summary: Venezuela admits citizens of the EU, the United Kingdom, Mexico and most of South America visa-free for up to 90 days when they arrive by air, while United States passport holders need a visa that has been very difficult to obtain since consular relations were suspended in 2019, and official travel advice is severe: the United Kingdom advises against all but essential travel and the United States says to reconsider travel, with both warning against any travel to the border regions.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave Venezuela; visa applications also need 6 months' validity. Venezuela extended the validity of its own citizens' passports by decree, which some airlines and third countries do not accept — a separate problem, but one that affects dual nationals.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from Brazil, or who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in Brazil. WHO also recommends vaccination for most travellers aged 9 months or over, except those staying only in Caracas, Valencia, Margarita Island and a few other low-risk areas.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement. WHO reports high malaria risk all year in parts of Amazonas, Bolívar, Delta Amacuro and Sucre states, moderate risk in Zulia and low risk in Anzoátegui and Monagas, and recommends prevention in risk areas. Take advice from a travel clinic before any trip outside the main cities.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry requirement, but the US State Department highly recommends it, including medical evacuation cover: hospitals are short of medical staff, medicines and equipment. Read a policy's exclusions for Venezuela before you rely on it.

currencyLimits.text: Declare cash or travellers cheques worth USD 10,000 or more when you enter Venezuela; tax is charged on the excess. Goods worth more than USD 1,000, personal luggage included, must also be declared.

notes: Drone equipment, satellite phones and professional camera gear draw scrutiny; journalists have been detained for filming without accreditation.
Airport departure taxes and fees are sometimes demanded in cash at the counter even when they are supposed to be included in the ticket.
Do not photograph airports, military installations, police or protests — cameras and phones have been confiscated.

payments.text: The economy is heavily dollarised after years of hyperinflation: US dollars in cash are accepted — and often preferred — for hotels, meals and taxis, while the bolívar loses value quickly and is used mainly for small change. Foreign cards are usually declined and international ATM withdrawals rarely work, so bring enough clean, small-denomination US notes for the whole trip.

safety.text: Official advice is severe. The UK advises against all travel within 80 km of the Colombian border and 40 km of the Brazilian and Guyanese borders, to Zulia state, the Orinoco Mining Arc and the area south of the Orinoco in Delta Amacuro, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the country. The United States rates Venezuela Level 3 (reconsider travel) for crime, kidnapping, terrorism and poor health care, and Level 4 (do not travel) for the Colombian border region, Amazonas, Apure, Táchira and Guárico states, Aragua outside Maracay and rural Bolívar. Violent crime, armed robbery and kidnapping occur; foreigners, including Europeans, have been detained and accused of terrorism, and arrivals can be held for hours or days for questioning. Power, water, fuel and medicine are often short, especially outside Caracas. After the June 2026 earthquakes La Guaira was declared a disaster zone under military control. Consular help is very limited.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Venezuela travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is the dry season, the practical window for Los Roques, Mérida and the Gran Sabana. Angel Falls is the exception. The boat trip up the Churún river needs the high water of the June-to-November wet season.

idp.text: Venezuela is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Check your own government's advice before doing anything else. The United States rates Venezuela Level 3 (reconsider travel), with Level 4 (do not travel) for the Colombian border region and several states, and the United Kingdom advises against all but essential travel to the country and against all travel to its border areas and Zulia. Travel insurance can be invalidated if you travel against your government's advice.

Venezuelan consular services in the United States have been suspended since 2019 and the US embassy in Caracas suspended operations in the same year; a phased resumption began in January 2026, but routine consular services remain suspended. US citizens who need a Venezuelan visa must apply through a Venezuelan consulate in a third country, and US emergency help is not available outside Caracas if something goes wrong.

Bring US dollars in cash — small, clean, undamaged notes. Foreign cards are generally refused, ATMs seldom pay out to international cards, and torn or marked bills are rejected. Do not rely on being able to get money once you are in the country.

Visa-free entry is not automatic for the full 90 days: the officer writes the number of days granted on the stamp, sometimes far fewer. Check it at the desk, because overstaying means fines and problems at departure.

Land borders with Colombia and Brazil open and close at short notice and the surrounding states are affected by armed groups and smuggling. If you must travel overland, check the crossing's status the same week and never move at night.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Venezuela?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the EU and EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Mexico and most South American countries enter visa-free for tourism when they arrive by air, for up to 90 days with a confirmed onward ticket. Canadian and United States passport holders need a visa, as does everyone not on the Foreign Ministry's exemption list — including Chile, Peru, Panama, Cuba and the Dominican Republic. Applications go through a Venezuelan embassy or consulate, and processing is slow and unpredictable.

faq.question: Can US citizens travel to Venezuela?
faq.answer: It is legally possible but practically difficult. The US government says to reconsider travel (Level 3) and not to travel to the Colombian border region and several states. A visa is required, and Venezuelan consulates in the United States have been closed since 2019, so applications must be made through a Venezuelan consulate in another country. The US embassy in Caracas has not yet resumed full operations: routine consular services are suspended and emergency help is not available outside Caracas. Confirm the current position with the Venezuelan Ministry of Foreign Affairs before making any plans.

faq.question: How long can visa-free visitors stay in Venezuela?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days per entry in principle, but the officer at the border writes the actual number of days on the stamp and often grants fewer. Extensions can be requested from the immigration authority (SAIME) inside the country, though the process is slow. Check your stamp before leaving the counter.

faq.question: What money should I take to Venezuela?
faq.answer: US dollars in cash. Years of hyperinflation have left the economy largely dollarised: hotels, restaurants and taxis quote and accept dollars, while the bolívar is used for small change. Foreign cards are usually declined and international ATM withdrawals rarely work, so bring small, clean notes covering the whole trip.

faq.question: Is Venezuela safe to visit?
faq.answer: No, not by ordinary standards. Violent crime, armed robbery and kidnapping occur, foreigners including Europeans have been detained and accused of terrorism, medicine, fuel and power are often short, and armed groups operate in the border states. The United Kingdom advises against all but essential travel to the country and the United States says to reconsider travel; travel insurance can be invalidated if you go against your government's advice.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Venezuela?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from Brazil: a certificate is required of travellers aged 1 or over coming from Brazil or after more than 12 hours' transit there. WHO also recommends vaccination for most of the country outside Caracas, Valencia and Margarita Island.
